tagline: From the cave country south over the hills to Tennessee.
intro: The highway starts at the entrance to Mammoth Cave National Park and runs out by KY 70 to Cave City, then KY 90 to Glasgow. South of town it takes KY 63 into Monroe County, twisting through hills and valleys to Tompkinsville and on to the Tennessee line.

It carries the name of Cordell Hull, born in a log cabin in Tennessee, who served longer than anyone as Secretary of State and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1945 for his part in founding the United Nations.

moments.title: Cave City
moments.text: The town is named for a cave inside its own limits, not Mammoth Cave ten miles west, and the railroad once drew its water from the creek that ran through that cave.

moments.title: Glasgow
moments.text: Named in 1799 for the Scottish hometown of a county commissioner's father, the county seat keeps the connection with Scottish Highland Games every year.

moments.title: Old Mulkey Meetinghouse
moments.text: Built in 1804 with twelve corners in the shape of a cross and three doors for the Trinity, the oldest log meetinghouse in Kentucky keeps Daniel Boone's sister Hannah in its graveyard.
